scope: Source-camera-frame bridge for the independent-chain boundary
summary: A real 80-frame continuation bridge was generated from source-camera frame 288 and safely adopted after a post-generation single-window QA bug, but neither tested stitch was acceptable as a complete long-video fix.
evidence: The bridge model loaded once and generated the 80-frame result in 73.3514 seconds; the raw result decodes at 624x351 and 24 FPS with SHA-256 7e42b31da806b914f9f77a163f7a54286f7ec17662f7c96a5b68c33e21c0240b.

The first launcher marked the completed result failed only because max() was applied to an empty single-window overlap list; the corrected fresh experiment verified and reused the immutable result by hash.
Radius-2 bridge stitching produced maximum transition ratio 5.9147; hard stitching produced 12.2147. Both remain review_required and do not improve on the non-bridge radius-4 maximum of 5.4317.
lessons: A local bridge conditioned on an aligned camera frame is insufficient when a later independently anchored chain remains in the output; long-horizon quality needs one dependency-preserving chain or regeneration of the entire downstream chain.
limitations: The bridge is only 3.33 seconds and does not itself constitute a 20-second-or-longer acceptance run.
Contact, exact action motion, and physical correctness remain unverified.
next_actions: Use a single rolling chain for the complete 27.5-second source and compare all nine overlap measurements against the two-chain result.
